mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.5% and remains above for at least two months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during three-month RSAFS declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 25 basis point or greater increase in the federal funds rate within a single month signals a tightening monetary stance, raising borrowing costs and discount rates, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by 0.25% or more in one month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline after a 25bp+ FEDFUNDS hike (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% and a decline in nonfarm payrolls for two consecutive months signals severe labor market stress, which reduces earnings and consumer demand, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.5% and PAYEMS declines for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when both UNRATE > 6.5% and PAYEMS declines for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and lower corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during three-month INDPRO declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand and residential investment, which reduces corporate revenue and profit growth, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when both RSAFS and HOUST decline for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for six consecutive months signals entrenched labor market weakness, which reduces earnings and consumer demand, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains above 6.5% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when UNRATE remains above 6.5% for six months (t-test p > 0.05).
